# Switch

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one setting that takes effect as it is turned on or off. For a choice the form sends
later, a Checkbox reads better. It is one element: Base UI's switch, as a native button.

```tsx
import { Switch } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="digest">Weekly digest</label>
<Switch id="digest" name="digest" defaultChecked />
```

**A name is required.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`), `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a Switch with none. The root is a `<button>` with
`role="switch"`, so the label names it in the server HTML and a click on the label presses it.
Switch draws no label of its own: you write it, and later a Field will.

**The state is `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange`**, Base UI's names. `value`
keeps its native meaning: the string the form receives when the switch is on (`on` by default).
Pass `checked` to control it. Your handler runs first, with Base UI's details, so
`details.cancel()` leaves the switch as it was.

```tsx
<Switch
  aria-label="Share my location"
  onCheckedChange={(next, details) => {
    if (next && !window.confirm('Share your location?')) details.cancel()
  }}
/>
```

**The form.** With a `name`, Base UI serves a hidden checkbox beside the button: off sends
nothing, on sends `name=on`, and `uncheckedValue` makes an off switch send that string. `form`
ties it to a form it is not inside. Before the page hydrates the form sends the default.
**A form reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form action that settles brings the switch back
to its `defaultChecked` of the latest render, on screen and in the form; a controlled switch
keeps its owner's value. A reset calls no `onCheckedChange`.

**`required` means "must be on"**, as on a native checkbox. Before the page hydrates, the
browser sends the focus of a blocked submit to the hidden input, a box of 1 px.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid`: the line of the track turns red and thickens. **`disabled`**
is the real attribute, so the switch leaves the tab order and the form sends nothing.
**`readOnly`** keeps it in the form and says so to a screen reader; it has no look of its own.

**The target is 24 px, 44 px under a finger**, whatever `size` draws: the focus ring is around
the track. `size="custom"` draws no track size: give the track one from your own CSS.

**In right-to-left** the thumb starts at the right and slides left.

**A wrapper** takes `SwitchProps`. `Omit<SwitchProps, 'x'>` merges the three ways to name a
switch into one where none is required.

### Recommendation on the state props (choice 2)

Keep Base UI's `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange` on Switch and Checkbox.
`R-5.7-1` asks for `value` and `onValueChange`, but on a toggle `value` is already the string
the form receives, as on a native checkbox, and `R-5.7-5` forbids renaming Base UI's props.
A boolean `value` would need that string under a new name and a hand-written handler.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Root`, `Thumb`, `role="switch"`, `aria-checked`, Space and Enter | as they are |
| `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names; the value is held for the form reset |
| `name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a `<span>` root | always a native `<button>`: `nativeButton` and `render` are not props |

### Not built

`tone` (one is drawn), a label, a hint and a required mark (a Field's), a hover look, a
read-only look, the invalid ring that is always on, text or an icon in the thumb, a loading
state, a skeleton (use `Skeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { Switch } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | Merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with the switch's own. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid, and the line of the track turns to danger and thickens. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The root element, which is a `<button>`. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The toggle scale of the track and its thumb; custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
